title: Pilot study investigating syndecan-1 and other endothelial damage markers in surgical patients
summary:
Damage to the cells lining the blood vessels can lead to problems before and after surgery. These include kidney failure, fluid accumulation in the lungs, and circulatory failure. Inflammation and stress caused by the procedure can also be contributing factors. Syndecan-1 is an important marker for the breakdown of glycocalyx. Before heart surgery, the value is approximately 50 ng/mL (SD ±15 ng/mL) and after surgery approximately 151 ng/mL (SD ±53 ng/mL). During cardiopulmonary bypass, the value can rise to up to 250 ng/mL. This is dangerous because it can lead to kidney failure. Secondary markers (heparan sulfate, hyaluronic acid, thrombomodulin, angiopoietin-2, MMP-2, MMP-9) indicate broader endothelial dysfunction. If there is too much fluid, the breakdown is intensified by natriuretic peptide. Research focuses on heart surgery. There is too little data for other types of surgery. This is detrimental to protective strategies such as optimized fluid management.
There is too little research on how syndecan-1 changes during surgery. The PEPC pilot study is investigating how syndecan-1 levels change during various types of heart surgery. The aim is to develop protective strategies against damage to the inner lining of blood vessels.

interventions.name:
Adult patients undergoing elective surgery, stratified in 4 groups: cardaic surgery, open surgery, laparoscopic surgery, and low-risk surgery.
Endothelial biomarker panel at three different time points: before surgery, one hour after surgery, and 24 hours after surgery. Endothelial biomarker panel:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective cardiac surgery (25 patients) Open surgery (all disciplines) (25 patients) Laparoscopic surgery (all disciplines) (25 patients) and low-risk surgery (all disciplines) (25 patients)

Informed consent (including broad consent for biobank).
Exclusion criteria:
Age <18 years.

• Emergency procedures.
• Incapacity to consent.
• Pregnancy.
• Operations <60 minutes.
• Outpatient procedures.
• Severe comorbidities (e.g., renal failure with GFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or liver failure with Child-Pugh C).
• Medications that affect the endothelium (e.g., high-dose corticosteroids).
